item1.justification: The §102 analysis uses element-by-element anticipation (checking each claim limitation against US-2012302167-A1) and the §103 analysis explicitly invokes Graham factors (scope and content, differences, PHOSITA level, secondary considerations) with KSR-compatible motivation-to-combine rationale throughout the obviousness stages.

item2.justification: Every rejection references specific claim language (e.g., 'automatic execution without user selection,' 'boot time engine start,' 'storing non-character input as drawing') and ties each conclusion to specific disclosures in US-2012302167-A1, such as 'generate a file including the generated output data' and lock-screen/gesture-based activation.

item3.justification: Claims found novel at §102 (7, 8, 10, 15, 20) are consistently treated as non-obvious at §103, while claims found not novel at §102 are rejected under §102 in the office action; the §103 rejections of claims 2, 7, and 15 are introduced with additional rationale not contradicting earlier novelty findings.

item4.justification: The examiner's high strictness (0.875) and low combination threshold (0.344) are consistently reflected: most claims are rejected under §102 on stretched but stated equivalences, §103 rejections are applied with minimal motivation requirements (e.g., 'routine data management,' 'automating a manual step'), and only three claims with clearly absent boot-time disclosure are allowed.

item5.justification: The final decision to reject claims 1–7, 9, 11–19 and allow 8, 10, 20 directly tracks the stage-level findings, with the summary explicitly tying each disposition to the §102/§103 analyses and identifying boot-time engine start as the non-obvious distinguishing feature.
